body.statement: For every \(\theta\in\mathcal T_K(r)\), let \(P^{\mathrm c}_{K,\theta}\) denote the law of \(\mathcal O_K^{\mathrm c}\) in \(\mathfrak I_K(\theta)\) and let \(P^{\mathcal F}_{K,\theta}\) denote its discrete finite-array law. After applying the measurable coarsening pushforward \(\mathsf Q_K\), \[\sup_{\theta\in\mathcal T_K(r)}\lVert P^{\mathrm c}_{K,\theta}\mathsf Q_K-P^{\mathcal F}_{K,\theta}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\le 2(n_0+n_1)/K^2,\qquad \sup_{\theta\in\mathcal T_K(r)}|L_K^{\mathrm c}-L_K|\le2(a+b)/K^2.\] Consequently the finite-collision decision transfers and the sparse Gaussian conclusion transfer at the actual endpoint \(L_K^{\mathrm c}\) whenever their displayed comparison errors vanish at the relevant unscaled or \(\sqrt{\lambda_K}\)-scaled level. This is a comparison of the coarsened pushforward with the discrete experiment; no total-variation comparison is asserted between raw continuous observations and discrete-label observations, and no conclusion is asserted beyond \(\mathcal I_K(r)\).
body.justification: The restricted transfer gives a continuous-covariate interpretation without claiming an unproved coarsening-bias theorem for a broad smoothness ball.
body.gap: Low and Zhou show that Poissonization transfer can fail below regularity thresholds; existing COT work does not justify this growing-roughness binary interpolation image.
body.consumer: The image supplies a controlled continuous stress test for \(\texttt{causalPIviaCOT}\) partition-resolution diagnostics.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(g^{\mathrm{step}}_{d,K,\theta}(u)=p_{d,\kappa_K(u)}\).  The union of the \(K-1\) interpolation strips has Lebesgue measure at most \(2(K-1)K^{-3}\le2K^{-2}\).  On a strip of half-width \(w=K^{-3}\), the integral of the absolute difference between the affine connector and the step function is one half of \(w|p_{d,j+1}-p_{dj}|\), and hence is at most \(a_dK^{-3}\), where \(a_0=a\) and \(a_1=b\).  Summing the strips gives
\[
 \int_0^1|g_{d,K,\theta}(u)-g^{\mathrm{step}}_{d,K,\theta}(u)|\,du
 \le\frac{a_d}{K^2}. \tag{28}
\]

Couple a continuous observation and its step version by using the same uniform \(U_{di}\), the same label \(\kappa_K(U_{di})\), and a common uniform random variable to generate the two Bernoulli outcomes.  The mismatch probability for one observation is the integral in (28).  A union bound over observations and then data processing by \(\mathsf Q_K\) yield the stronger estimate
\[
 \sup_\theta
 \lVert P^{\mathrm c}_{K,\theta}\mathsf Q_K-P^{\mathcal F}_{K,\theta}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\frac{n_0a+n_1b}{K^2}
 \le\frac{2(n_0+n_1)}{K^2}. \tag{29}
\]
In the opposite direction, a parameter-free kernel that adds an independent uniform position within each observed cell turns the discrete experiment into the step experiment; the same coupling proves the corresponding deficiency bound in (29).  This is a comparison through kernels, not a claim that probability measures on the raw, different sample spaces have a direct total-variation distance.

The binary extremal-coupling calculation from the endpoint proposition applies pointwise in \(u\), so
\[
 L_K^{\mathrm c}=\int_0^1|g_{1,K,\theta}(u)-g_{0,K,\theta}(u)|\,du.
\]
The reverse triangle inequality and (28) give
\[
 |L_K^{\mathrm c}-L_K|
 \le\sum_{d=0}^1\int_0^1
 |g_{d,K,\theta}-g^{\mathrm{step}}_{d,K,\theta}|\,du
 \le\frac{a+b}{K^2}
 \le\frac{2(a+b)}{K^2}. \tag{30}
\]
Both bounds are uniform in the signs.

Composing any discrete rule with \(\mathsf Q_K\), or any continuous rule with the uniform-within-cell reverse kernel, changes a bounded risk or a coverage probability by at most the error in (29); expanding an interval by the target error in (30) and using the full-interval repair preserves honesty.  Under finite collision intensity these errors vanish because \(n_0+n_1\le K^2\varepsilon_K/(n_0n_1)\le K^2\varepsilon_K\).  In the sparse Gaussian regime, (30) is negligible after multiplication by \(\sqrt{\lambda_K}\), since \(\lambda_K/K\to0\), while (29) still tends to zero because \((n_0+n_1)/K^2\le\varepsilon_K\).  Thus the finite-collision decision conclusions and the sparse Gaussian conclusion transfer at the actual \(L_K^{\mathrm c}\) under their stated error conditions.  The construction and both kernels are defined only on \(\mathcal I_K(r)\), so no extension to a larger smoothness class is asserted.
